alex_m: Heads-up — noticed a perf regression on the microqueue path after yesterday's kernel swap. p99 for long sequences jumped ~80ms, p95 mostly unchanged. GPU util climbed to ~96% during the spike. Anyone seen KV miss rate change around the same window?

mike_infra: saw the canary traces. kv_miss_rate had a short burst at 12:37UTC, coinciding with a GC on the KV pool. logs show repeated kvcache eviction/rehydration around that time.

tara: can you paste the minimal flamegraph / perf counters? even small snippet helps.

alex_m: sure — pasted a tiny excerpt from the profiler:
```
# p99 tail sample
kernel: aten_attn_opt_v2
microbatch_size: auto (avg 14 -> spikes to 28)
kv_hit_ratio: 0.81 -> dips to 0.56 during spike
gpu_util: 78% -> 96% during spike
latency_p95: 120ms
latency_p99: 205ms (was ~125ms)
```

jess_cohen: hypothesis: the new kernel has a different memory layout that performs worse on partial-KV-hit scenarios. When many requests have small prefixes, kv miss + kernel layout causes more mem copies and longer tail.

srini: +1. Also microbatch auto-sizing reacts to queue depth; when kernel latency increases it ups batch size which amplifies tail. two feedback loops: kv_miss -> kernel slowdown -> batching upsizes -> GPU saturates -> headroom collapses -> p99 spikes.

emma: I ran a short A/B on canary route /chat/infer:
- control (old kernel, microbatch cap 16): throughput 420r/s, p95 118ms, p99 132ms, gpu_util 79%
- candidate (new kernel, microbatch auto): throughput 384r/s, p95 122ms, p99 206ms, gpu_util 95%
So we lose tail even if avg throughput is close.

perf-bot: perf-regression alert: route=/chat/infer p99 +74.2ms since deploy 2045410000.

alex_m: tradeoff: option A reduce kernel change (fallback to old kernels for cached-heavy routes); option B keep kernel but limit microbatch cap and add soft-admit when GPU>85%; option C aggressive kvcache prefetch/warm to reduce misses. Thoughts?

jess_cohen: Option B seems least invasive. Implement soft-admit policy: if gpu_util > 85% and p95>target, start shedding best-effort low-priority requests and cap microbatch at 12. I'll prototype admission rule and a config flag `admission.soft_cap=0.85` and `microbatch.cap=12` for canary. @mike_infra can you wire the canary? :thumbsup:

mike_infra: will schedule 10-min canaries for both changes after lunch. I'll also expose kv_miss_rate and kernel_latency as SLO tags in the canary dashboard.

tara: also suggest adding a lightweight metric: per-kernel per-prefix memcpy count. would help prove memory-layout hypothesis.

srini: if prototype confirms, we should add a rollout policy: default to soft-admit for customer tiers without strict latency SLO, and keep old-kernel for p99-sensitive routes. maybe implement model-routing by `route.performance_profile`.

emma: quick note — prefetch helps but increases vram usage; if we prefetch aggressively we'll need to account for headroom. so prefetch + soft-admit might be the balanced play.

alex_m: plan: jess to prototype admission + microbatch cap, mike to run A/B canaries, tara to add memcpy counters, srini to draft rollout policy. Follow-up in #eng-runtime in ~4h with results. thanks everyone. :rocket:
